name: Li Jingmin
current_role: Chairman, general manager and controlling shareholder, Linzhou Fengbao Pipe Industry Co. (Fengbao Special Steel group), Henan
profile: Linzhou, Henan native (b. 1969) and mechanical engineering graduate who was recruited in 2001 by Fengbao founder Li Guangyuan and became general manager of Fengbao Special Steel at about 32. She now controls Linzhou Fengbao Pipe Industry, a seamless steel tube maker spun out of the group in 2007 that had about RMB17bn revenue in 2022.
interesting_fact: Fengbao Pipe ranked 447th on the 2023 China Manufacturing Private Enterprise 500 list, and the 2023 profile describes it as Anyang's only private company on those lists.
deep_cut_fact: She studied mechanical engineering at Taiyuan Institute of Machinery (now North University of China), and under her the plant commissioned what was billed as the world's first six-stand small-diameter three-roll continuous seamless tube rolling unit (2017).
notes: Low public profile. Source is a single promotional Sohu article (Oct 2023), so facts are not independently verified. Hurun lists the company as 'Fengbao Iron & Steel' (凤宝, not 丰宝). No published personal or press contacts found. Any outreach would have to go through the company in Linzhou, in Chinese.

name: KP Ramasamy
current_role: Founder and Chairman, KPR Mill Ltd and KPR Group (Coimbatore, India)
profile: Born into a farming family in Kalliampudur village, Erode district, he started as a power-loom cloth maker in 1971 and, with his brothers, built KPR Mill into one of India's largest vertically integrated apparel makers, with sugar, ethanol, power and education arms. He still chairs the group and appears on Forbes India's rich lists.
interesting_fact: KPR Mill runs an in-house higher-education program for its mostly rural women workers. The company says about 27,000 employees have earned degrees (computing, management, nursing, teaching) while working there, through tie-ups with Annamalai, Alagappa and Tamil Nadu Open universities.
deep_cut_fact: He started his first power-loom business in 1971 with a borrowed Rs 8,000, which some profiles say came from his mother's uncle.
notes: Also appears as Palanisamy Ramasamy Kalliampudur on data sites. The published email is the company's investor-grievance address, not a press line, so the corporate office in Coimbatore is the realistic route. The group also has an energy angle: windmill/solar and sugar-ethanol cogeneration.

name: Jill S Wyant
current_role: President & CEO and Director, Madison Air Solutions Corp (NYSE: MAIR). Also a director of Dow Inc. and Vice Chairman of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce board.
profile: A former GE and Ecolab executive (EVP and President, Global Regions and Global Healthcare at Ecolab), she has run Madison Air, Madison Industries' air-quality platform, since June 2021. In April 2026 she took it public in a $2.2bn IPO, reported as the largest US industrial IPO since 1999. Its brands include Big Ass Fans, Broan-NuTone and Nortek Data Center Cooling.
interesting_fact: Madison Air's $2.2bn IPO in April 2026 was billed as the biggest US industrial listing in decades. Wyant pitched data centers, chip fabs and hospitals as key growth niches, and the company owns Nortek Data Center Cooling.
deep_cut_fact: Her undergraduate degree from the University of St. Thomas was in International Marketing and Japanese Studies. She later earned an MBA with highest honors from Chicago Booth.
notes: Strong fit for a data-center or energy podcast because of data-center cooling. The media contact listed on Madison Air press releases is the best route.

name: Sumitra Agarwal
current_role: Director in the Delhi-branch Haldiram's companies (e.g. Haldiram Marketing Pvt Ltd), per company-registry aggregators; current status unclear
profile: A member of the Delhi-based Agarwal family behind Haldiram Snacks, who appeared on the Hurun India Rich List in 2019. Registry aggregators list her (DIN 00011417) as a director of Haldiram Marketing, Haldiram Ethnic Foods and Haldiram Snacks entities. No public biography or media profile was found.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's traces back to a sweets shop opened in Bikaner in 1937 by Ganga Bhishen 'Haldiram' Agarwal. Hurun has named Haldiram Snacks India's most valuable unlisted company (about Rs 63,000 crore, 2024).
notes: Very private, with no interviews or social accounts found. Her exact place in the family and her current directorships could not be confirmed: aggregators disagree, and one shows her Haldiram Marketing role ending in Jan 2026. Any contact would go through the Haldiram's corporate office. Low priority.

name: Avishai Abrahami
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Wix.com Ltd (Nasdaq: WIX). Director, monday.com.
profile: A Jerusalem-born serial entrepreneur and IDF Unit 8200 veteran who co-founded Wix in 2006 with his brother Nadav and Giora Kaplan, after the founders were frustrated by how hard it was to build websites. He has grown Wix into a global website-building platform for tens of millions of users and is now pushing it into AI-built sites. He was also an early backer and board member of monday.com.
interesting_fact: Wix was monday.com's first customer, and Abrahami was an early investor who owned about 4% of monday.com at its 2021 IPO. Founder Roy Mann credits him with helping them 'identify the challenge of harnessing people at work.'
deep_cut_fact: Before Wix he founded the software company AIT in 1994 and sold it in 1997, then co-founded Sphera Corporation (1998), which was later acquired by SWsoft. Wikipedia also says he practices ninjutsu.
notes: Wix PR (pr@wix.com) is the best route. The ninjutsu detail rests on Wikipedia only, so treat it lightly. Strong entrepreneurship guest.

name: Vijay Biyani
current_role: Unclear. Formerly Managing Director of Future Retail (from May 2016) and a senior executive at Future Enterprises.
profile: Vijay Laxminarayan Biyani is a brother of Kishore Biyani and one of the Biyani family members who built the Mumbai-based Future Group (Big Bazaar, Pantaloons heritage), India's former retail giant. He served as Managing Director of Future Retail and on the boards of group companies, and appeared on the Hurun India Rich List in 2018-19.
interesting_fact: Future Retail redesignated Vijay Biyani as its Managing Director in May 2016, during the group restructuring in which Kishore Biyani became vice chairman.
notes: Future Retail and the group's listed companies went through insolvency proceedings from 2022, so there is no working corporate press channel. No personal public presence was found. Avoid the group's financial troubles in any outreach. Low priority.

name: N Nagaraju
profile: Listed on the Hurun India Rich List 2019 with wealth attributed to 'personal investment'. No public source was found that identifies which N. Nagaraju this is, so no profile was compiled.
notes: Ambiguous name (common South Indian name), and the Hurun entry gives no company. Could not determine who this is, so the profile is left minimal. Skip unless Hurun's 2019 list entry can be checked directly.

name: Michael O'Grady
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Northern Trust Corporation (Chicago). Director, Abbott Laboratories.
profile: Michael G. O'Grady (60) was a Bank of America Merrill Lynch investment banker who joined Northern Trust as CFO in 2011. He then ran its Corporate & Institutional Services arm, became President in 2017, CEO in 2018 and Chairman in 2019. He leads the bank's 'One Northern Trust' strategy, and it reported 2025 revenue of about $8.1bn.
interesting_fact: He moved from outsider to CEO in about seven years: hired from BofA Merrill's investment banking group as CFO in 2011, he was running the 130-plus-year-old Chicago custody and wealth bank by 2018.
notes: Best route is the Northern Trust media contacts listed on its 2026 press releases. Web search quota ran out during this lane, so no deep-cut fact was sourced.

name: Rehan Jaffer
current_role: Founder and Managing Member, H Partners Management LLC (New York investment firm). Director, Six Flags Entertainment Corp since May 2026.
profile: Founder of H Partners Management, a concentrated, long-term public-equity investor. He joined the Six Flags board after the 2026 annual meeting under a cooperation agreement with the company, replacing H Partners' previous representative Arik Ruchim, and sits on its Audit and Finance Committee.
interesting_fact: According to Six Flags' filing, H Partners had been a significant Six Flags investor for more than 15 years and long had a seat on its board before Jaffer took it himself in 2026.
notes: Low-profile hedge fund founder. The listed contacts are Six Flags company channels, not his own. A better route would be H Partners itself, but no official website or contact for it was confirmed (web search quota ran out). The 8-K URL was built from the filing's accession number.

name: Keith Stuart Liddell
current_role: Founder and Chair of the Board, Lifezone Metals Ltd (NYSE: LZM)
profile: A metallurgical engineer who has worked only in minerals and metals since 1981, taking nickel, copper and PGM projects from exploration through to production. He founded the Lifezone group, which listed on the NYSE via a SPAC in 2023. As chair he focuses on its Hydromet refining technology and the Kabanga Nickel Project in Tanzania. He and his family hold about 28% of Lifezone.
interesting_fact: Lifezone's pitch is its own hydrometallurgical ('Hydromet') process, offered as a lower-emission alternative to smelting, which it plans to use to refine nickel from the Kabanga project in Tanzania.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a minerals engineer, with an honours BSc in Minerals Engineering from the University of Birmingham and an MSc in Engineering from the University of the Witwatersrand. Lifezone also retains him as a consultant for hands-on metallurgical engineering.
notes: Good fit for an energy-transition and critical-minerals (battery nickel) episode. The company's general info@ address is the only published channel found.

name: Morgado Horta Alessandro Monteiro
current_role: Founding partner, CEO and Director, Vinci Compass Investments Ltd (Nasdaq: VINP), Rio de Janeiro
profile: Alessandro Monteiro Morgado Horta (55) is a founding partner of Vinci Partners, which grew out of Banco Pactual's principal investment group and merged with Chile's Compass Group to form Vinci Compass, a Latin American alternative-asset manager. Before Vinci he was managing partner and COO at Banco Pactual, a VP at UBS Pactual, and a partner at Banco Icatu.
interesting_fact: Vinci Compass is consolidating Latin American asset management. In October 2025 it agreed to buy 50.1% of Verde Asset Management, Luis Stuhlberger's multi-strategy firm with about R$16bn in assets.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an electrical engineer at PUC-Rio, like co-founder Gilberto Sayao. At Banco Pactual (2001-06) he was managing partner and COO and also ran the Long-Term Investments division.
notes: Known publicly as Alessandro Horta. The SEC insider record lists him as 'Pres. of Finance & Operations', but the 2025 20-F names him CEO. Best route is the US PR agency (Prosek).

name: Marcus G Smith
current_role: CEO, Speedway Motorsports LLC. Director and 10% owner, Sonic Automotive Inc. (NYSE: SAH).
profile: Son of motorsports and auto-retail pioneer Bruton Smith. Marcus Smith worked his way up from sales associate at Charlotte Motor Speedway to President (2008) and CEO (2015) of Speedway Motorsports, which owns 11 racetracks. He took the company private in 2019 and is also a major shareholder and director of Sonic Automotive, the car-dealership group his father founded.
interesting_fact: He led the revival of the long-abandoned North Wilkesboro Speedway, one of NASCAR's founding tracks, after a 2019 push from Dale Earnhardt Jr. and others. The track returned to grassroots racing in 2022 and hosted the NASCAR All-Star Race from 2023.
deep_cut_fact: As a high schooler at Charlotte Country Day, where he was a wrestler, he volunteered at Charlotte Motor Speedway doing grass maintenance, painting walls and picking up trash. He had planned to become a doctor at UNC-Chapel Hill before joining the family business.
notes: Visible, fan-facing CEO. The best route is Speedway Motorsports' communications team, but no published press email was found (web search quota exhausted). The Sonic IR address comes from a 2023 release. Avoid the Bristol, Atlanta and track-repave criticism.

name: Viswas Raghavan
current_role: Head of Banking (investment, corporate and commercial banking) and Executive Vice Chair, Citigroup
profile: 'Vis' Raghavan is an India-raised investment banker who spent 24 years at J.P. Morgan, mostly in London, rising from equity-linked capital markets to global co-head of investment banking. CEO Jane Fraser recruited him to Citi in 2024 to run its combined banking businesses, and he has since brought over about 15 senior bankers to rebuild Citi's M&A franchise.
interesting_fact: Citi offered a reported $40m package to hire him from J.P. Morgan in 2024, and he is widely seen as a potential successor to Jane Fraser.
deep_cut_fact: He studied physics at the University of Bombay before earning a dual degree in electronic engineering and computer science at Aston University in Birmingham, UK, and started his banking career at Lehman Brothers. He is also a keen professional-cricket follower.
notes: Rarely gives interviews. Requests would go through Citi corporate communications (newsroom). No published press email was found in recent Citi 8-K releases.

name: Tina P Johnson
current_role: Trustee of Publix's 401(k) Plan stock, member of Publix's ESOP Committee, and trustee/co-trustee of large trusts holding Publix stock (Publix Super Markets, Lakeland FL)
profile: Her SEC '10% owner' status at employee-owned Publix comes mostly from fiduciary roles. The 2026 proxy shows her as trustee over about 278m Publix shares in the 401(k) Plan, an ESOP Committee member, and trustee or co-trustee of trusts holding about 75m shares in which she has no pecuniary interest. Her direct holdings are roughly 0.55m shares.
interesting_fact: Publix is one of the largest employee-owned companies in the US: its ESOP owns about 21% of the stock and its 401(k) Plan about 8.7%, and Johnson helps oversee how those shares are voted.
notes: The 'wealth' figure is likely overstated: most of the reported shares are held as trustee without pecuniary interest. No public profile, title or bio was found, so this looks like a fiduciary or administrative insider rather than a business founder. Not a natural podcast guest. Any contact would go through Publix corporate communications.

name: Marvin R Ellison
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, Lowe's Companies (since 2018; Chairman since May 2021). Director, FedEx.
profile: A career retail operator who spent 15 years at Target and 12 at Home Depot (rising to EVP of U.S. Stores), then served as CEO and Chairman of J.C. Penney (2015-18). He joined Lowe's as CEO in 2018 and has focused on store operations, the Pro customer and digital and omnichannel growth.
interesting_fact: He is one of very few executives to have held senior roles at both Home Depot and its archrival Lowe's: after 12 years at Home Depot overseeing U.S. stores, logistics and Pro initiatives, he became Lowe's CEO.
deep_cut_fact: His path to the top ran through the back of the store: at Home Depot he was VP of Loss Prevention before moving to VP and then SVP of Logistics, after starting his career in operational roles at Target in 1987.
notes: High-profile CEO, so the route is Lowe's corporate communications via its newsroom. The media emails on older releases date from 2022 and may be stale, so they were omitted.
